**Software Engineer - Delivery Search**
  
  
**About the Role**
  
  
We are seeking talented Software Engineers to join our Search Engineering team and help build the next generation of AI-powered search experiences across Uber Eats, Grocery, and Retail.
  
  
In this role, you will build and improve large-scale backend systems that power search retrieval, ranking, query understanding, and emerging LLM-based search experiences. You will work on high-throughput, low-latency services that retrieve and rank relevant restaurants, stores, dishes, and items from large catalogs in real time.
  
  
You will collaborate closely with backend and ML engineers, data scientists, product managers, and platform teams to improve search quality, latency, scalability, and reliability. You will have opportunities to work across traditional search infrastructure, semantic retrieval and machine learning, as well as emerging LLM-powered retrieval, ranking, and search experiences.
  
  
**About the Team**
  
  
The Delivery Search team builds the core search technology behind Uber Eats, Grocery, and Retail. We work across the search stack, including query understanding, indexing, lexical and semantic retrieval, ranking, model serving, and search serving infrastructure.
  
  
Our work combines large-scale distributed systems, information retrieval, machine learning, and increasingly LLMs and generative AI to solve challenging problems around relevance, latency, scalability, and reliability. The team owns systems serving millions of users and is evolving the search stack toward more intelligent, real-time, and AI-powered architectures.
  
  
**Basic Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
* 2+ years of professional software engineering experience building and delivering production systems.
* Proficiency in at least one programming language such as Go, Java, C++, or Python.
* Experience developing backend services, APIs, or distributed systems.
* Understanding of core computer science concepts, including data structures, algorithms, concurrency, and system design.
* Experience writing maintainable, well-tested production code.
* Strong problem-solving skills and ability to collaborate effectively with engineers and cross-functional partners.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience building scalable, high-throughput, or low-latency backend systems.
* Familiarity with search, recommendation, information retrieval, ranking, or ML-powered systems.
* Familiarity with LLMs, generative AI, or ML model-serving systems and an interest in applying them to large-scale search.
* Experience with embeddings, semantic retrieval, approximate nearest-neighbor search, or vector search.
* Experience building or integrating LLM-powered applications, retrieval/ranking systems, or evaluation pipelines.
* Familiarity with model-serving or inference concepts such as batching, caching, streaming, or latency optimization.
* Experience with search technologies such as Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Solr, Vespa, Lucene, or similar retrieval systems.
* Familiarity with distributed systems and technologies such as Kafka, Redis, Cassandra, Spark, or Flink.
* Experience with performance optimization, monitoring, observability, and production debugging.
* Experience working on large-scale consumer-facing products.

**What the Candidate Will Do**

* Build and maintain scalable backend services powering search across Uber Eats, Grocery, and Retail.
* Develop retrieval and ranking systems that help customers find relevant restaurants, stores, dishes, and items.
* Build and productionize LLM- and ML-powered search capabilities, including query understanding, retrieval, ranking, and emerging generative search experiences.
* Work with lexical retrieval, semantic retrieval, embeddings, and ML/LLM-based ranking to improve search relevance.
* Partner with ML engineers and data scientists to integrate machine-learned and LLM-based models into production search serving paths.
* Build scalable search serving and indexing infrastructure capable of handling high query volumes and large catalogs.
* Improve system latency, throughput, reliability, and infrastructure efficiency across retrieval, ranking, model serving, and data hydration.
* Contribute to infrastructure supporting efficient model inference, caching, batching, and streaming for latency-sensitive search experiences.
* Analyze search and system performance, debug production issues, and identify opportunities to improve relevance and serving performance.
* Build observability and reliability mechanisms and participate in the operational ownership of production search systems.
* Participate in design and code reviews and contribute to technical decisions for well-scoped projects.
* Write clean, reliable, well-tested, and maintainable production code.
Collaborate with Product, Data Science, ML, and other engineering teams to ship customer-facing search improvements.  

  
  
For San Francisco, CA-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $171,000 per year - USD $190,000 per year.  
  
For Sunnyvale, CA-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $171,000 per year - USD $190,000 per year.  
  
For all US locations, you will be eligible to participate in Uber's bonus program, and may be offered an equity award & other types of comp. All full-time employees are eligible to participate in a 401(k) plan. You will also be eligible for various benefits.  
  
**Ready to Ride?**  
  
This isn't the kind of place where you follow a playbook - it's where you help write one. If you're driven by impact, energized by challenge, and ready to shape how the world moves - we'd love to hear from you.  
  
You may be eligible for bonuses, equity, and other compensation, as well as a range of benefits. Explore our benefits.  
  
Offices remain key to collaboration and Uber's culture. Unless approved

jobs.description:
Human Computer Lab is a research lab building character robots that feel alive and responsive. Our first robot, LeLamp, explores a new category of consumer robotics where everyday objects become interactive and help us reshape our attachment to technology.

Our goal is to push the frontier of human-robot interaction by making technology more legible, emotionally intuitive, and human-centered. We are building the foundation for a new generation of robots designed for everyday environments.

**What to expect**

We're looking for an inventor who builds. Someone who gets an unlikely idea on a weekend, tries it, watches it fail, notices something surprising in the wreckage, and follows that instead - all the way to a model, a dataset, a working robot, and a write-up anyone can reproduce. Research is the inventing half: finding the question nobody has asked, trying the unexpected method first, and building the evaluation that tells you the truth. Engineering is the making half: turning the idea into something that runs on a real robot, in a real home, fast enough that a person never notices the machinery. Most people are strong at one. This role is for the person who can't stop doing both. It isn't bound to one discipline - the problem might be expressive motion this month, sensing or thermals next quarter, an inference stack or a new robot body after that. You'll work directly with the CEO and founding team, with real room to explore, on problems that ship to people's homes.

**In this role, you will:**

* Pick open problems across the system - motion, perception, sensing, actuation, thermals, inference, tooling - and take them from first idea to working artifact.
* Try the unlikely approach before the obvious one, kill it honestly when it fails, and use what the failure taught you.
* Build the evaluation before you trust the result: the metric, the probe, and the side-by-side that catch what averages hide.
* Create data where none exists - bootstrap it, synthesize it, curate it with taste - and know when synthetic data is misleading you.
* Ship end to end: the model, the dataset, the firmware, the demo, and the robot in the room. Make it fast and reliable enough for everyday life.
* Work across abstraction layers when the problem demands it — from a circuit or motor driver up to a trained model and the interaction on top of it.
* Write up what you tried, what failed, what the numbers say, and what you'd do next, so someone else can reproduce it.
* Use AI as a research collaborator - to map a search space, run experiments, and pressure-test your own ideas - and share your judgment in how you use it for novel approaches.

**You may be a good fit if you:**

* Have a body of self-directed work - projects, repositories, write-ups, videos, robots - that you started because you were curious, not because it was assigned. This matters more to us than any credential.
* Have taken at least one idea from “what if” to a working, measured artifact, end to end.
* Are fluent in Python and comfortable further down the stack - C/C++, embedded, or electronics — or have a record of learning a new layer when a problem required it.
* Have trained, evaluated, and deployed ML models, and can reason about latency and compute on edge devices.
* Have built real hardware - a robot, a device, an instrument, a sensor rig - from parts, not from a kit.
* Can explain your failures as clearly as your successes.
* Have a degree in engineering, computer science, physics, or a related field, or equivalent proof of work.
* Have published research, open-source projects people actually use, or a public body of technical writing. A plus, not a requirement.

**You will be a strong fit, if you:**

* Can't stop doing both halves — inventing the method and building the thing — and get restless doing only one.
* Choose problems as carefully as you solve them, and can tell an interesting question from a merely difficult one.
* Report what you found, not what you hoped. You'd rather say “it passed these checks” than “it's solved.”
* Have taste. You care whether something feels alive and reads right to a person, not only whether the loss went down.
* Move fast without being sloppy, and leave every result reproducible.
* Care about what technology does to people - not just what it can do and want your inventions to change how people relate to the machines in their lives.

The early team becomes the DNA of the company. We set ourselves and others to a high standard, and we respond with kindness when things get hard but keep everyone accountable. This requires us to be curious, creative, and diverse in our thinking and approach.
  
  
We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. Even if you don’t meet every single requirement, we encourage you to apply. Studies show that women and underrepresented groups often hold back unless they meet 100% of the criteria - we don’t want that to be the reason we miss out on great talent.

San Francisco, in-person 4x/week

**About Luzid**

Luzid is building the operating system for SAP delivery — the infrastructure layer underneath the most complex and expensive IT projects companies run. SAP implementations move billions of dollars and thousands of consultants, but the knowledge generated in these projects is never captured: it lives in people's heads, disappears when the project ends, and gets rebuilt from scratch on every new engagement.

Luzid solves this with an agentic orchestration platform that coordinates every phase of SAP transformation, capturing decisions, tests, and context as a byproduct of work already underway — building an organizational memory that accumulates across projects instead of resetting.

We're a team based in San Francisco and São Paulo, moving fast and already deployed with some of the largest SAP integrators in the world, including delaware Consulting, KPMG, and NTT Data. We have reached >$3M ARR in 11 months and raised $21M in funding. The team comes from Stanford, Meta, Two Sigma, Microsoft, and NASA.

**The Opportunity**

You'll build the interfaces consultants and enterprise teams use to navigate complex implementations and work with AI agents. These workflows involve substantial information, interconnected decisions, and work that unfolds over time. Your job is to make that complexity understandable and manageable through thoughtful, responsive software.

You'll work closely with design and other engineers, and talk directly to customers to understand where they're encountering friction. You'll help shape what we build, prototype alternatives, ship improvements, and follow through on how they perform in production.

Your primary focus will be the frontend: both the experiences users interact with and the foundations that help our team build them well. You'll have room to make consequential technical decisions and the responsibility to keep them practical — using AI-assisted development tools to explore and iterate, while applying your own judgment to the quality and simplicity of what we ship.

**What You'll Do**

* **Own product outcomes.** Take ambiguous problems from customer conversations through implementation, deployment, and iteration.
* **Build the core interfaces.** Ship the experiences consultants and enterprise teams use to navigate complex implementations and work with AI agents.
* **Reason from UX back into implementation.** Decide which interactions need to feel instantaneous, how state and data should flow, and when a problem calls for a better component, a different loading strategy, or a change to an API.
* **Design for real usage.** Think through loading, empty, error, and recovery states; collaborate closely with design; treat accessibility as part of a complete experience.
* **Build durable foundations.** Recognize reusable interaction patterns, design clear component APIs, and use composition and shared primitives to keep the product consistent as it grows.
* **Make the product feel fast.** Reason about rendering, network requests, caching, prefetching, and feedback during longer operations — and measure whether changes actually help.
* **Work across boundaries.** Reason about APIs, data models, and backend behavior when they affect the frontend, and make pragmatic build-vs-use calls.
* **Raise the team's bar.** Work independently, communicate decisions clearly, and improve the experience of engineers building alongside you — including how the team uses AI-assisted workflows.

**What We're Looking For**

* **Deep frontend fundamentals.** You've shipped and maintained complex interactive applications, and understand JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML and CSS, browser behavior, rendering, state management, and asynchronous data flow.
* **Strong UX judgment.** You think in terms of how people will actually use a feature, not just whether it works.
* **Evidence-driven.** You combine customer feedback with analytics, performance monitoring, and session replay to identify friction and evaluate the impact of changes.
* **Ownership.** You ask questions, challenge assumptions, and care whether what you shipped actually helped, not just whether it shipped.
* **Pragmatism.** You know when to use an existing library, when custom implementation is worthwhile, and how to balance immediate delivery with longer-term maintainability.
* **Curiosity and judgment.** Above all, you understand problems deeply, explore possible solutions, and make thoughtful trade-offs between user experience, engineering quality, speed, and complexity.

**Nice to have**

* Experience building interfaces for AI-powered products, including workflows where users review, guide, or approve agent actions.
* Experience evolving a component library or design system while continuing to ship product features.
* Experience on a small team where you helped shape product and design decisions alongside engineering.
* Familiarity with complex enterprise workflows or ecosystems such as SAP, Salesforce, ERP, or CRM.

**Why Join Luzid Now**

* Shape the interfaces for a product with proven traction inside the largest SAP integrators in the world — delaware Consulting, KPMG, and NTT Data — in a category being defined right now.

### **Company Description**

**Join us and make YOUR mark on the World!**

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has turned bold ideas into world-changing impact advancing science and technology to strengthen U.S. security and promote global stability.

Research will focus on integrating large-scale multiomic datasets, including bulk, single-cell, spatial, and multimodal data, from animal models and human cohorts to identify molecular programs associated with disease progression, immune responses, and biological resilience. Define what “better” means for representations that evolve over time.

Continuously evolve evaluation definitions as models and product capabilities change.

3+ years of professional experience designing and owning LLM evaluations.

Human Computer Lab is a research lab building character robots that feel alive and responsive. Our first robot, LeLamp, explores a new category of consumer robotics where everyday objects become interactive and help us reshape our attachment to technology.

Our goal is to push the frontier of human-robot interaction by making technology more legible, emotionally intuitive, and human-centered. We are building the foundation for a new generation of robots designed for everyday environments.

**What to expect**

We're looking for an inventor who builds. Someone who gets an unlikely idea on a weekend, tries it, watches it fail, notices something surprising in the wreckage, and follows that instead - all the way to a model, a dataset, a working robot, and a write-up anyone can reproduce. Research is the inventing half: finding the question nobody has asked, trying the unexpected method first, and building the evaluation that tells you the truth. Engineering is the making half: turning the idea into something that runs on a real robot, in a real home, fast enough that a person never notices the machinery. Most people are strong at one. This role is for the person who can't stop doing both. It isn't bound to one discipline - the problem might be expressive motion this month, sensing or thermals next quarter, an inference stack or a new robot body after that. You'll work directly with the CEO and founding team, with real room to explore, on problems that ship to people's homes.

**In this role, you will:**

* Pick open problems across the system - motion, perception, sensing, actuation, thermals, inference, tooling - and take them from first idea to working artifact.
* Try the unlikely approach before the obvious one, kill it honestly when it fails, and use what the failure taught you.
* Build the evaluation before you trust the result: the metric, the probe, and the side-by-side that catch what averages hide.
* Create data where none exists - bootstrap it, synthesize it, curate it with taste - and know when synthetic data is misleading you.
* Ship end to end: the model, the dataset, the firmware, the demo, and the robot in the room. Make it fast and reliable enough for everyday life.
* Work across abstraction layers when the problem demands it — from a circuit or motor driver up to a trained model and the interaction on top of it.
* Write up what you tried, what failed, what the numbers say, and what you'd do next, so someone else can reproduce it.

**Software Engineer, Frontend**

**About Luzid**

Luzid is building the operating system for SAP delivery — the infrastructure layer underneath the most complex and expensive IT projects companies run. SAP implementations move billions of dollars and thousands of consultants, but the knowledge generated in these projects is never captured: it lives in people's heads, disappears when the project ends, and gets rebuilt from scratch on every new engagement.

Luzid solves this with an agentic orchestration platform that coordinates every phase of SAP transformation, capturing decisions, tests, and context as a byproduct of work already underway — building an organizational memory that accumulates across projects instead of resetting.

We're a team based in San Francisco and São Paulo, moving fast and already deployed with some of the largest SAP integrators in the world, including delaware Consulting, KPMG, and NTT Data. We have reached >$3M ARR in 11 months and raised $21M in funding. The team comes from Stanford, Meta, Two Sigma, Microsoft, and NASA.

**The Opportunity**

You'll build the interfaces consultants and enterprise teams use to navigate complex implementations and work with AI agents. These workflows involve substantial information, interconnected decisions, and work that unfolds over time. Your job is to make that complexity understandable and manageable through thoughtful, responsive software.

You'll work closely with design and other engineers, and talk directly to customers to understand where they're encountering friction. You'll help shape what we build, prototype alternatives, ship improvements, and follow through on how they perform in production.

Your primary focus will be the frontend: both the experiences users interact with and the foundations that help our team build them well. You'll have room to make consequential technical decisions and the responsibility to keep them practical — using AI-assisted development tools to explore and iterate, while applying your own judgment to the quality and simplicity of what we ship.

**What You'll Do**

* **Own product outcomes.** Take ambiguous problems from customer conversations through implementation, deployment, and iteration.
* **Build the core interfaces.** Ship the experiences consultants and enterprise teams use to navigate complex implementations and work with AI agents.
* **Reason from UX back into implementation.** Decide which interactions need to feel instantaneous, how state and data should flow, and when a problem calls for a better component, a different loading strategy, or a change to an API.
* **Design for real usage.** Think through loading, empty, error, and recovery states; collaborate closely with design; treat accessibility as part of a complete experience.
* **Build durable foundations.** Recognize reusable interaction patterns, design clear component APIs, and use composition and shared primitives to keep the product consistent as it grows.
* **Make the product feel fast.** Reason about rendering, network requests, caching, prefetching, and feedback during longer operations — and measure whether changes actually help.
* **Work across boundaries.** Reason about APIs, data models, and backend behavior when they affect the frontend, and make pragmatic build-vs-use calls.
* **Raise the team's bar.** Work independently, communicate decisions clearly, and improve the experience of engineers building alongside you — including how the team uses AI-assisted workflows.

**What We're Looking For**

* **Deep frontend fundamentals.** You've shipped and maintained complex interactive applications, and understand JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML and CSS, browser behavior, rendering, state management, and asynchronous data flow.
* **Strong UX judgment.** You think in terms of how people will actually use a feature, not just whether it works.
* **Evidence-driven.** You combine customer feedback with analytics, performance monitoring, and session replay to identify friction and evaluate the impact of changes.
* **Ownership.** You ask questions, challenge assumptions, and care whether what you shipped actually helped, not just whether it shipped.
* **Pragmatism.** You know when to use an existing library, when custom implementation is worthwhile, and how to balance immediate delivery with longer-term maintainability.
* **Curiosity and judgment.** Above all, you understand problems deeply, explore possible solutions, and make thoughtful trade-offs between user experience, engineering quality, speed, and complexity.

**Nice to have**

* Experience building interfaces for AI-powered products, including workflows where users review, guide, or approve agent actions.
* Experience evolving a component library or design system while continuing to ship product features.
* Experience on a small team where you helped shape product and design decisions alongside engineering.
* Familiarity with complex enterprise workflows or ecosystems such as SAP, Salesforce, ERP, or CRM.

* Shape the interfaces for a product with proven traction inside the largest SAP integrators in the world — delaware Consulting, KPMG, and NTT Data — in a category being defined right now.
* Own consequential technical decisions on a small, senior team, with a short line between an idea and it being in production.
* Build the frontend foundations for a company at $3M+ ARR after 11 months, backed by $21M in funding, with a team from Stanford, Meta, Two Sigma, Microsoft, and NASA.
